Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates near-complete opacification of the right hemithorax with a contralateral (leftward) mediastinal shift, which is the classic radiographic presentation of a massive pleural effusion pushing structures away due to volume overload. In contrast, atelectasis would cause an ipsilateral shift, and pneumothorax would typically show hyperlucency rather than opacity.
